claim: Figure S2 labels two different compounds VN3C2
locus_A: Fig S2 panel (e): "VN3C2 HRMS calc. for C71H123N2O6+ [M+H]+: 1099.9376"
locus_B: Fig S2 panel (g): "VN3C2 HRMS calc. for C71H121N2O6+ [M+H]+: 1097.9220"
what_we_emitted: Panel (e) emitted as VN3C2. Panel (g) emitted under the placeholder name "PANEL-G (label disputed)" with NO value attached to it.
why: The two formulas differ by exactly H2, so at most one of the two labels is right. Panel (g)'s formula is VN2C4 + CH2 to 0.05 mDa and the figure-S5 legend lists a VN2C3 that has no HRMS panel, so (g) is most likely VN2C3 or VN3C4 - but mass cannot choose between a 2-carbon linker with a piperidine head and a 3-carbon linker with a pyrrolidine head, which are both C7H16N2. Not resolved.

claim: Figure S4b's printed correlation for DMG-PEG is negative
locus_B: Table S2 DMG-PEG mol% vs our 58 digitised bars: Spearman +0.5324 (p=1.7e-05), Pearson +0.5811
what_we_emitted: Nothing. We emit no correlation; the discrepancy is recorded only.
why: The other three printed coefficients reproduce to |delta| <= 0.016 on Spearman (VN2C2 -0.636 vs -0.6275; DDAB -0.501 vs -0.5170; Chol +0.727 vs +0.7215), which both identifies the unstated metric as Spearman AND validates our bars. DMG-PEG reproduces to 0.013 IN MAGNITUDE with the sign inverted. No parameterisation of Table S2 yields a negative coefficient: mol% +0.532, rank +0.532, share-of-its-block +0.299, Chol/DMG-PEG ratio -0.296 (wrong magnitude). The design is collinear in the direction that forces the positive sign: corr(Chol, DMG-PEG) = +0.23 and Chol itself is +0.72. Most consistent with a sign typo in the printed table.

locus_A: Fig S1a caption: "Structure diagram of 35 common commercial amino small molecules"
locus_B: Fig S1a draws 35 entries but CAS 7209-38-3 (1,4-bis(3-aminopropyl)piperazine) appears twice, at row 1 col 1 and row 6 col 1, with identical structures - 34 DISTINCT
what_we_emitted: We record 35 drawn entries and 34 distinct CAS numbers.
why: Counted by transcribing every CAS label at 3x upscale and hashing. One library slot is therefore unaccounted for, which is suggestive given that VN2C1's core amine is absent from the drawn set - but a duplicate drawing is not evidence about which amine is missing.

claim: The lead compound's core amine is in the screened library
locus_A: Fig S1 caption: "Screening and construction of VNxCyOz lipid library" over the 35 drawn amines
locus_B: Fig S2 panel (h) pins VN2C1 at C68H117N2O6+, whose core is C4H12N2; NO drawn amine has that formula (nearest are 107-15-3 C2H8N2 and 111-41-1 C4H12N2O)
what_we_emitted: VN2C1 emitted with NO structure and NO corpus row, despite being the paper's lead compound in Figures S8, S12, S13 and all in-vivo work.
why: Same for VN3C2O, whose core C7H18N2O2 is one CH2 longer than both drawn bis(hydroxyethyl) amines. So the drawn set is demonstrably not a complete inventory of the cores used, which is why no structure in this paper is treated as pinned.

claim: Figure S4b's y axis is 'Luciferase expression (%)' with a 0-150 range
locus_B: Lip3000 reads 102.0% and Naked siRNA 99.9%; no treated LNP exceeds 92.6%
what_we_emitted: Values as measured; Lip3000 and Naked siRNA are marked corpus_admissible=no as control arms.
why: Naked siRNA at 99.9% is the implied 100% reference the panel never prints, and it lands 0.15% off - an unprinted round-number check that the calibration passes. Lip3000 at 102.0% is above it, which is possible for a transfection control but is recorded because a normaliser above its own reference is worth a reader seeing.
